reviews.text: If you're a fan of strategy games, this one is incredibly addictive. Its well-designed mechanics and engaging gameplay will keep you hooked for hours. Definitely worth investing your time in this!

The demo was alright the rest is not. Dev said the length of the game should be around 3.5h which makes it a bit expensive. Then again, I'm all in for supporting indie devs but... - You can not get your demo data to the game. -Using the mouse to move is great and all, but having the movement speed limited makes it more frustrating than anything. Upgrades that increase movement speed only makes you feel "alright" until you try to move your mouse a bit too quick and get back to that "hampered" feeling. - The pacing of the game is really slow, even slower than the demo, it's like the dev want you to at least spend 2h before finishing the game. - The upgrade are mostly stats based and there isn't much to truly change the gameplay. - Most upgrade are blocked until you do a lot of the same one around, so the tree is quite directive. Also it's not like you can make a choice since most upgrade are hidden until you get close to them anyways... - A lot of the time you can't advance even being goodl, you just have to die and grind...a lot! Overall I'm a bit sad, I had high hopes for the game because the first few minute feels great and novel, but there isn't much more to see. Note: At the time of posting (1h45 after release), there are two positives review saying that you can complete the game using differents paths (did they get the game earlier? since they wouldn't have the time to complete it...). This sounds weird since the upgrade tree is quite directive. Both of them have only ever made 2 reviews, one has a private profile, the other is friend with the devs. ~o~

Super grindy, I hate how you start at 0 minutes each time because at this point I breeze past the first minute and die within about 10 seconds after the first minute. So I'm basically just waiting for a minute each time I start a session and it's pretty boring at this point. Some of the upgrades just require you to constantly play again and again, barely getting any better just to accrue more upgrades, the progression is unreasonably slow. Also, the performance is nuts, I get frequent (as in every few seconds) micro-stutter/micro-hitches in the game. I'm playing with a 4090/7800X3D/64GB DDR5. It's nuts that this game, so focused on smooth movement, is getting such constant micro-stutter. I had high hopes for this game, wishlisted it since I first saw it on r/incremental_games, but man is this disappointing. I love fast paced incremental games with huge skill trees, it's a shame

DO BETTER, DEVELOPER, DO BETTER!... PATHETIC! GET GOOD! This game insults you ever time you lose... and you're going to lose a lot, because it's a bullet hell, but you're in a tiny box with a slow movement speed. It's also a very buggy game prone to crashing. The upgrades feel underwhelming and the manual, that tells you how to play, also insults you. Well screw you developer. You don't deserve mine, or anyone else's money. You ask people to pay money for your game, then you call them pathetic for not playing it very well. When the game doesn't even have the decency to play properly. There are some phenomenal games out there that insult you, but they've earned the right to. This game has not, it doesn't earn the right to insult you, it doesn't even earn the right to be bought by you. I strongly recommend against buying this. Pathetic game. Thanks for reading, or skipping to the end, have a lovely day. Edit: The developer posted about the game, and said it's an idle game. Don't be confused, this is a bullet hell, not an idle. Update: I gave the game a bit more time. (Initial review I gave it 6 minutes. I've now given it over an hour.) I still hate this game... It does eventually stop insulting you as much. But the bullets just get ridiculously fast, there's even bullets that move erratically later. It's... just not a fun time. I wish I could refund it, but I got it as part of a bundle, something I won't be doing again as I've been screwed over a lot by these steam bundles.

Holy crap this gets so repetitive and boring. The moment you reach purple and start upgrading, the progression almost halts. You get max +5 second more each run just to get 1 or 2 upgrades and repeat again. When I hit 2 minutes and did not get a new resource, I just said ♥♥♥♥ this. Because I knew I had to go through another 10+ games of the exactly same thing to do any sort of progression.

The game has something there, but in its current iteration is simply not worth the $8.5AUD price point. It took about 3 hours to complete and obtain the perfect clear on achievements (there are additional challenge modes if you're into that). The game suffers from a pacing problem, it is incredibly badly paced at the start and mid points and then once it finally does it fun the game ends in the next 25 minutes. It's ironic that the game ends right when it feels like it finally starts. The issue with it is that each upgrade tier takes far too many runs to get to, but the problem is that these runs simply don't feel fun. The problem lies with the game having an identity crisis.. it doesn't know if it wants to be a roguelite or an incremental game. Unlike other roguelikes where you want to go again because you feel like you have a shot at potentially ultra instincting it and doing a god run, this game just does not have that because you know it is impossible to progress.. it has the roguelike resets but the incremental growth where the only way to get stronger is to play longer/do more runs but the runs in and of itself are so boring. The reason why i say that the game only starts to feel fun at the end is that you're finally at the point where you're unbounded and now have access to actual abilities to use.. but by then you're literally on the final stages of the game and it simply ends.. the first 2hours is literally just playing till the game forces you to die, over and over and over again. It's designed so that the game ramps up to a point where you will die, no matter how well you play, and you're forced to hit that wall 4-5 times to grind enough currency to get the upgrade that lets you survive, then you hit the next wall 4-5 times until the next one, over and over again, all the while playing a base game mechanic that is simply unfun.

The concept is interesting but there are some design and balance problems that mean I can't recommend purchasing this game. The main problem is that in the mid-to-late game, there's a significant mismatch between the tokens you're earning and the skills you're spending them on. There is a market you can use to trade tokens for other types but this is just papering over an underlying issue with the design and balance of the skill tree. Maybe this was a skill issue but progressing to the last token took far longer than it felt like it should, to the point where I almost gave up and uninstalled because I was not making any progress. Once the last token was unlocked, the game's difficulty suddenly dropped hard. This game could be pretty good if the skill tree were rebalanced.

[h1]More of a warning review[/h1] While it is positive - most of it comes from me having fun trying to get it running on win 7 machine back in the days (its actually a [b]chromium[/b] (browser) engine game and win7 support is dropped lmao) and [b] being somewhat competent at bullet hell[/b] genre, which is being crossed over with incrementals quite frequently, idk. Progressing through this [b]WILL take some skill[/b] mid-game, because while early upgrades can be grinded for - next currencies will be gained after reaching 1:00 and 2:30 survival marks to spawn new enemies which provide these currencies, and "start from X minute mark" upgrades are quite a far reach. Upgrades themself are a mixed bag: there are skills that you can use in game to help with dodging projectiles, but they're absolutely useless early on, you have to commit to maxing one out to be able to [b]properly[/b] utilize it, otherwise it might just not be equipped. This principle can apply to some other upgrades, like temporary invincibility. [hr][/hr] This game might ask too much of you to keep the progression pace in tact as the developer intended, so if you expect an incremental here - make sure you can handle bullet hell too, since there are at least 2 stopcaps (new resource gain minute marks) that might frustrate you out of this game because there's really no way around it other than "git gud".

This is a fun little incremental for what it is, and i still definitely recommend it despite a few standout flaws. I love how the tree unlocks new nodes via upgrading those around them in whatever order you want, both partially and sometimes fully. The "story" slipping in as you play and coming to the realization yourself at a certain point is also a neat addition. I love the challenges too, and even managed to beat the no movement one! But the other two are either extreeemely hard or impossible to complete a full 5 minutes of. Having an achievement for the one I did would be very satisfying, but I don't know if i could get myself to go for the other two. As for my problems, income can be annoyingly slow at times, and the prices in the tree aren't balanced around that very well. Especially at the end of the game, the top left and bottom right corners take foreeeever to get enough to buy them. While I enjoy how the tree opens, especially with unlocking new resources, later on some upgrades you really want are either hidden behind ones you don't or take way too much investment to open up at all. The last thing I'll add is the "boss fight" option on the main menu feels pretty worthless. The first isn't challenging at all and the other two don't look fun to try, and I don't feel a need to without incentive.
